title: 1. The arc of the market: from the agora to the stationary state, and what the texts do to that story
md:
**The hypothesis.** The market was first a place and an occasion ordered by officials; then an ethical problem; then the scholastics' just price (*pretium iustum*, a range set by common estimation); then the merchant's own knowledge; then the state's ledger (mercantilism); then a self-regulating order (Boisguilbert to Smith); and finally a machine of *improvement* (making land, work and knowledge yield more; Bacon to Babbage), with its critics (Sismondi to Marx).

**The verdict, in short.** As a list of when each idea is first *argued at length in European print*, the sequence mostly holds. As a story of one idea replacing the last, or as a story of the whole world, it fails in four places.
- **The state's market comes first, not fifth.** The *Guanzi*, the Salt and Iron debate, the *Arthashastra* and Xenophon's *Poroi* already treat price as an instrument of the ruler. Mercantilism added the balance-of-trade ledger and the habit of counting, not the idea that the state works through the market.
- **The just price was, for the most part, already the market price.** Aquinas lets a seller take "the price he finds", and the Salamancans tie the just price to the common estimation of a particular place and day. Stage 3 is where the market's price becomes morally authoritative. It is not where the market becomes self-governing: the same texts keep the legal price and condemn monopoly.
- **The self-correcting market appears first as profit-and-exit and fluid levels, not as providence.** Ibn Khaldun has it around 1377; the English pamphlets of 1690–91 have it in print. Smith's *invisible hand* is a late, local and conditional statement of an idea already a century old in English.
- **"Self-ordering" and "wealth-creating without limit" are different ideas with different lineages.** The political economists who made the market self-ordering (Smith, Malthus, Ricardo, Mill) all expected a *stationary state*, where accumulation stops. Open-ended growth was thinkable earlier and elsewhere: in Bacon and the Royal Society's useful knowledge, in Barbon's "Stock of a Nation Infinite", and in Mercier's world that "goes by itself". The two did not fully merge before 1867.

**How to read the ids.** Ids without a prefix are claims in this concept. `harmony-kb:` and `aliveness-kb:` ids are claims already held by those concepts; they are cited here, not copied. Partial (◐) claims are hedged; unverified (○) ones are not used. Dates are dates of *writing* where the claim records one.

## Where the market was located, period by period

| Period | Main site | Other sites already present | Key claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classical Greece (5th–4th c. BCE) | a **place** (the *agora*, the civic square that was also the market) and a **household** art (*oikonomia*, household management) | the city's revenue (Poroi); moral suspicion of retail | [[7]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-rep-agora-nomisma-symbol), [[8]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-laws-no-citizen-retailer), [[9]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-xen-poroi-prizes-market-officials), [[10]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-natural-acquisition-has-limit) |

| Islamic, c. 1100–1400 | the **place** policed by the *muḥtasib* (holder of the *ḥisba*, the office of commanding good and forbidding wrong in the market), and money as the "judge" between goods | an impersonal order of taxes and city prices (Ibn Khaldun) | [[26]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ghazali-money-as-judge), [[27]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-hisba-office), [[28]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-maqrizi-muhtasib-cairo-1341), [[29]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields), [[30]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-city-prices) |

## The arc, stage by stage

### 1. The market as a place, ordered by officials: confirmed, but never only that

The agora appears in Plato as the thing a city of divided producers needs once they buy and sell, with coin as a "token" of exchange [[7]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-rep-agora-nomisma-symbol). Rome's *nundinae* joined the market day to the day laws were heard [[23]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/roman#anc-macrobius-nundinae-market-and-law). The officials are real: Xenophon would give prizes to the market officials who settle traders' disputes fastest [[9]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-xen-poroi-prizes-market-officials); Ibn Khaldun files the *ḥisba* among the religious offices [[27]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-hisba-office); al-Maqrizi records a Cairo *muḥtasib* in 1341 parading a trader whose poultry had rotted in store [[28]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-maqrizi-muhtasib-cairo-1341). But in each of these texts the place already carries more: in Xenophon it carries the city's revenue [[70]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-xen-poroi-metics-best-revenue), and in Plato a law that no citizen may be a retailer [[8]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-laws-no-citizen-retailer). "Place" is never the whole of the concept, even at the start.

### 2. Exchange as an ethical problem: confirmed, but the objection is to *retail and usury*, not to exchange

Aristotle's objection is narrower than its reputation. Exchange is natural: a shoe has two uses, and exchange began because some had more than they needed [[11]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-shoe-two-uses-exchange-natural). What has no limit is *chrematistike* (the art of acquisition) made an end in itself [[10]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-natural-acquisition-has-limit), and what is most against nature is *tokos*, money born of money [[12]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-tokos-money-begets-money). The invisible-hand article's "money is barren" turns this round; the page says money *gives birth* to money, which is the offence [[71]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#anc-crit-article-aristotle-barren). Plato says retail would be honoured "like a mother and a nurse" if it were incorruptible [[72]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-laws-retail-honourable-if-incorruptible); Cicero grades *mercatura* (trade) by scale, sordid when small, tolerable when large [[24]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/roman#anc-cicero-off-small-trade-sordid-great-tolerable). The Chinese texts make the same cut between root and branch: Confucius and Mencius set *yi* above *li* [[18]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-analects-yi-li-4-16), [[19]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-mencius-1a1-why-say-profit), and the literati of 81 BCE ask that "branch profit" be suppressed [[17]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-yantie-literati-suppress-branch-profit). Their opponent, however, is not the merchant but the state's own trading monopolies, which is not *laissez-faire* in any modern sense [[73]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#anc-crit-literati-not-laissez-faire) ◐. The moral problem lasts: Aquinas still finds in *negotiatio* (buying to sell dearer) "a certain baseness" [[32]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-trade-baseness), and in 1640 Saumaise still had to answer the dictum that a merchant can never please God [[74]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-saumaise-negotiator-never-pleases-god).

### 3. Just price and the measure of value: the decisive move is here, earlier than the arc implies

Aristotle had already made money a conventional measure and a guarantor of future exchange [[13]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-ne-money-measure-by-convention), [[14]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-ne-money-guarantor-future-exchange). Al-Ghazali makes it a "judge" with no colour of its own, like a mirror [[26]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ghazali-money-as-judge). Aquinas prices things by human use, not their rank in nature [[75]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-price-by-human-use), puts the just price in a range set by estimation [[31]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-just-price-estimation), and, in the case of the merchant who knows more ships are coming, lets him sell at "the price he finds" without disclosure [[76]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-seller-price-he-finds). That formula reached the confessors' manuals [[77]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-pisanella-repeats-aquinas-estimation). The Salamancans make the *communis aestimatio* the measure outright: Molina against nature or nobility [[39]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-molina-price-from-estimation-not-nature), Soto by the number of buyers and the fair [[41]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-soto-buyers-and-fairs-move-price), Mercado at the place and moment of delivery [[40]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mercado-just-price-at-place-of-delivery), Grotius by what is "commonly" given [[78]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#emod-grotius-common-price-latitude). Molina and Azpilcueta treat money as a merchandise whose abundance raises prices [[42]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-molina-money-abundance-raises-prices), [[79]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-azpilcueta-cambios-money-scarcity-price); Azpilcueta calls this the common view "of almost all Christendom", so the article's priority over Bodin is overstated [[80]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-azpilcueta-money-is-merchandise). Oresme's money belongs to the community, not the prince [[34]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-money-not-princes), and bullion leaves a debased kingdom whatever is forbidden [[81]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-bullion-flees-debasement). The "Gresham's Law" reading is his 1864 editor's [[82]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#med-oresme-gresham-is-wolowskis). On de Roover's reading the scholastic just price was ordinarily the market price [[83]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#med-crit-deroover-just-price-is-market-price) ◐; Koehn and Wilbratte argue it is the price a just person would accept [[84]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#med-crit-koehn-just-person-price) ◐.

The limit is just as clear. The same texts keep a legal price, condemn monopoly and collusion, and hold the civil and the divine law apart [[85]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#emod-critique-estimation-not-laissez-faire), [[86]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-soto-monopoly-iniquity), [[87]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mercado-merchant-collusion), [[88]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mercado-civil-law-tolerates-divine-law-forbids). The market's price became *just* in stage 3. It did not become *self-governing*.

### 4. The merchant's own knowledge: confirmed, but it is not a theory of the market

Pegolotti is a table of places, weights and coins [[35]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/merchant-practice#emod-pegolotti-merchant-knowledge-measures); Cotrugli gives the journal, the ledger and the trial balance [[36]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/merchant-practice#emod-cotrugli-bookkeeping-journal-ledger-balance) (his priority over Pacioli rests on a 1458 manuscript, and SL's "Pacioli" is a 1994 paraphrase). Cotrugli derives trade from need and money "as from a living fountain" [[89]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/merchant-practice#emod-cotrugli-money-source-of-mercatura). Scaruffi dreams of one world money of account [[38]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/mercantilism#emod-scaruffi-universal-money-of-account). This is know-how and bookkeeping; it does not ask what the market as a whole does. The one text in this layer that does is not European: Ibn Khaldun defines commerce, without reproach, as buying cheap to sell dear [[90]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-commerce-defined).

### 5. The state's market: real, but not new

Mun's balance of trade is "the rule of our Treasure" (written c. 1622–30) [[43]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/mercantilism#enl-mun-balance-rule); Petty counts in "Number, Weight, and Measure" [[44]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/mercantilism#enl-petty-number-weight-measure); Steuart in 1767 still addresses a statesman who lays down a plan [[91]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-steuart-statesman-plan). But the *Guanzi* had said *qingzhong* has no fixed numbers and one responds as things arise, and a state that cannot draw in the world's wealth cannot be made [[15]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-guanzi-qingzhong-no-fixed-number); Han officials bought cheap and sold dear to break the great merchants [[16]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-yantie-comm-pingzhun-buy-cheap-sell-dear); the *Arthashastra*'s superintendent watches demand and fixes margins [[20]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/indic#anc-arth-superintendent-commerce-demand-price), [[21]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/indic#anc-arth-fixed-profit-margin); Pliny counts the bullion drain to the East [[25]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/roman#anc-pliny-nh-luxury-drain-sesterces). The Chinese debate is in effect the mercantilism debate seventeen centuries early ([[92]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#anc-mod-weber-guanzi-state-market-participation) ◐). What *is* new in 17th-century England is the ledger and the arithmetic, and a patent law that rewards "new manufactures" [[45]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-statute-of-monopolies-new-manufactures). Cameralism (Becher, Justi, Sonnenfels) and Colbert have no claims yet.

### 6. The self-regulating market: earlier, and first mechanical rather than providential

The first texts in this concept that describe the market as correcting itself without an official are:
- Ibn Khaldun (c. 1377): higher tax rates yield less because people stop working [[29]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields); the state is "the great market" whose hoarding slackens all the rest [[93]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-state-greatest-market); a trading ruler crowds out his subjects [[94]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-ruler-trading-harms); city prices are the sum of households' behaviour [[30]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-city-prices).
- Oresme (c. 1355): good coin leaves a debased realm "despite all prohibitions" [[81]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-bullion-flees-debasement), and merchants shun it [[95]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-merchants-shun-bad-money). Mariana (1599): Alfonso XI's price ceiling "was in vain" [[96]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mariana-debasement-futile-price-control).
- North's *Discourses* (1691): no trade can be unprofitable to the public, "for if any prove so, men leave it off" [[47]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-unprofitable-trade-left-off); the whole world as to trade is "but as one Nation" [[48]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-world-one-nation). Locke (1691/92): the law cannot hold interest below its "natural" rate [[49]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-locke-natural-interest).

The vocabulary then multiplies. Boisguilbert: "Nature breathes only liberty" [[51]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/physiocracy#enl-boisguilbert-nature-breathes-liberty). Cantillon: prices settled by "altercation" [[52]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-cantillon-price-by-altercation) and production run by *entrepreneurs* (who buy at a certain price to sell at an uncertain one) "au hazard" [[97]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-cantillon-entrepreneur-au-hazard). Hume: money finds its "proper level" like a fluid [[53]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-money-proper-level). Mercier (1767): "the world then goes by itself" [[54]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/physiocracy#enl-mercier-monde-va-de-lui-meme). Ferguson (1767): "the result of human action, but not the execution of any human design" [[98]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-ferguson-human-action-not-design). Smith's Glasgow lectures (c. 1763): "the best police" (*police*: the regulation of a state's trade and provisioning) is to leave things to their natural course [[99]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-lj-best-police-natural-course). In 1776 come the division of labour as the slow consequence of a propensity to truck [[100]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-propensity-truck), the butcher's self-love [[101]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-butcher), and the *invisible hand* [[55]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-invisible-hand). The image appears in TMS (1759) as well ([[2]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#econ-smith-1759-invisible-hand), [[3]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#econ-smith-1759-harmonious-movement-of-system)).

Three things complicate the "self-regulating" stage.
- **It was not uncontested, even at its height.** Mandeville's vices become benefits only "by the dextrous Management of a skilful Politician" [[102]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-mandeville-skilful-politician); Quesnay's *Tableau* *assumes* full liberty and secure farm capital rather than showing that they arise [[103]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#enl-quesnay-tableau-assumes-liberty); Steuart's statesman appears in the same year as Ferguson and Mercier [[91]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-steuart-statesman-plan).
- **Smith's *invisible hand* is narrow.** In WN it concerns preferring domestic to foreign *industry* (in 1776, labour employed, not manufacture), and Rothschild reads the *laissez-faire* prophet as a later myth ([[104]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#enl-crit-rothschild-invisible-hand) ◐).
- **The end of zero-sum thinking runs alongside it, and earlier.** Barbon (1690) says trade "hath occasioned Peace" [[105]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-trade-occasioned-peace); Montesquieu (1748) gives *doux commerce* (gentle commerce, which softens manners) [[106]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-montesquieu-doux-commerce) but adds that commerce unites nations, not individuals [[107]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-montesquieu-peace-not-individuals); Hume (1758) prays, "as a British subject", for the flourishing commerce of Germany and France [[108]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-jealousy-of-trade); Du Pont says the natural order of commerce gives no motive for war [[109]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/physiocracy#enl-dupont-natural-order-no-war). Hirschman's account of interests taming the passions frames this ([[110]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-hirschman-passions-interests) ◐), and Hume's case for governing men by "avarice and industry" fits it [[111]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-commerce-avarice-industry).

### 7. Improvement and the Industrial Revolution: two lines that met late

**The improvement line** starts outside political economy. Bacon makes new inventions and resources the goal of the sciences [[46]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-goal-of-sciences), and names printing, gunpowder and the compass as having changed the world more than any empire [[112]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-three-inventions). His Salomon's House aims at "the Effecting of all Things possible" [[56]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-salomons-house). Hartlib pairs "Improvement" with experiment [[57]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-hartlib-experiment-improvement). Sprat plans histories of every trade [[113]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-sprat-history-of-trades) and argues that saving hands by invention increases riches [[58]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-sprat-saving-hands-riches). Barbon's "Stock of a Nation Infinite" (1690) [[50]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-national-stock-infinite) and Mandeville's ships and watches built by divided labour and "the Experience of many Generations" (1729) [[114]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-mandeville-1729-division-of-labour) carry the open horizon into economic writing.

**The political economists kept a ceiling.** Smith's progressive state is cheerful and the *stationary state* dull, but the *stationary state* is still where the "full complement of riches" ends [[59]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#ind-smith-stationary-dull). Malthus frames the age's question as "illimitable" improvement against oscillation, and answers oscillation [[115]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-malthus-illimitable-or-oscillation). Ricardo's profits "gravitate" downward, checked only at intervals by machinery [[60]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-profits-gravitation), and he trusts England is "yet far distant" from the *stationary state* [[116]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-stationary-far-distant). Mill (1848) accepts that the increase of wealth is not boundless, and then separates the two ideas this concept follows: a *stationary state* of capital and population, he says, implies no stationary state of human *improvement* [[62]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-mill-stationary-state). Read together: [[63]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-classical-stationary-horizon). The great analytical gains are real but sit inside that horizon: comparative advantage [[117]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-comparative-advantage), Babbage's principle [[66]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-babbage-principle) and the division of mental labour [[118]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-babbage-mental-labour) (see [[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-mechanism-babbage)). Say's denial of a general glut is the one classical text that removes a ceiling on the demand side [[64]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-say-debouches). The most open-ended voice of the 1840s is a protectionist: List's productive powers "for eternal times" [[119]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-list-industrial-education).

**The critics argued with the change as it happened.** Ricardo retracted his view of machinery in 1821 [[61]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-on-machinery); Sismondi blamed Say and Ricardo for the gluts [[65]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-sismondi-engorgement); Carlyle named the "Mechanical Age" in 1829 [[120]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-carlyle-mechanical-age) and refused "Cash-payment" as "the sole nexus" in 1843 [[68]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-carlyle-cash-nexus). Ure's factory withdraws every delicate process from the "waywardness of workmen" [[67]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-ure-self-acting-factory), and Marx answers him: "not only as an automaton but as an autocrat" [[121]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-marx-ure-automat-autokrat). Marx's M–C–M, buying in order to sell [[69]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-marx-g-w-g), is Aristotle's unnatural acquisition and Aquinas's "baseness" restated as the defining form of capital (compare [[10]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-natural-acquisition-has-limit), [[32]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-trade-baseness)). Bastiat's harmony of interests is held in harmony ([[5]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/economics#econ-bastiat-creed), [[6]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/economics#econ-bastiat-conditional)); here he appears only for joining machine-breaking to protection [[122]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-bastiat-machine-breaking-protection).

## Turn points

| When | What turned | Claims |
|---|---|---|
| 4th c. BCE – 81 BCE | price as the ruler's instrument, argued as policy | [[15]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-guanzi-qingzhong-no-fixed-number), [[16]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-yantie-comm-pingzhun-buy-cheap-sell-dear) |
| c. 330 BCE | exchange natural, acquisition unlimited, money a convention | [[11]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-shoe-two-uses-exchange-natural), [[13]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-ne-money-measure-by-convention) |
| c. 1270 | the just price as an estimated range; the seller may take "the price he finds" | [[31]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-just-price-estimation), [[76]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-seller-price-he-finds) |
| c. 1355 | money belongs to the community; coin flees debasement | [[34]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-money-not-princes), [[81]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-bullion-flees-debasement) |
| c. 1377 | taxes, city prices and the state's spending reasoned as an impersonal order | [[29]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields), [[93]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-state-greatest-market) |
| 1550s–1590s | just price = common estimation at a place and day; money a merchandise | [[39]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-molina-price-from-estimation-not-nature), [[40]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mercado-just-price-at-place-of-delivery), [[42]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-molina-money-abundance-raises-prices) |
| 1620–1667 | useful knowledge and invention as the source of riches | [[46]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-goal-of-sciences), [[45]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-statute-of-monopolies-new-manufactures), [[58]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-sprat-saving-hands-riches) |
| 1690–1692 | the self-correcting market and the end of zero-sum trade, in English print | [[47]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-unprofitable-trade-left-off), [[50]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-national-stock-infinite), [[49]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-locke-natural-interest) |
| 1752–1776 | levels, altercation, "il va de lui-même", the invisible hand | [[53]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-money-proper-level), [[54]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/physiocracy#enl-mercier-monde-va-de-lui-meme), [[55]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-invisible-hand) |
| 1817–1829 | machinery, gluts and the Mechanical Age argued while they happen | [[61]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-on-machinery), [[65]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-sismondi-engorgement), [[120]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-carlyle-mechanical-age) |
| 1867 | buying in order to sell named as the form of capital | [[69]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-marx-g-w-g) |

## Verdict on the hypothesised arc

| Stage | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 place | **holds, with a caveat** | real in every tradition, but never only a place |
| 2 ethical problem | **holds, narrowed** | the target is retail, usury and unlimited acquisition, not exchange as such |
| 3 just price | **holds, and carries more weight than the arc gives it** | the market's price becomes the just price; it does not become self-governing |
| 4 merchant knowledge | **holds as practice, not as theory** | Ibn Khaldun, not the Italian manuals, is the theorist of commerce |
| 5 the state's market | **misplaced** | ancient in China, India and Greece; what is new c. 1620 is the ledger and the arithmetic |
| 6 self-regulation | **holds, but earlier and more mechanical** | Ibn Khaldun c. 1377 and the English 1690s precede Smith; contested at its height |
| 7 improvement | **two lines, not one** | the Baconian line is open-ended; the political economists keep a *stationary state* until Mill |

The order of stages 5 and 6 also fails *within* Europe. Mun's balance (c. 1625), North's self-correction (1691), Steuart's statesman (1767) and Mercier's world that "goes by itself" (1767) overlap; these are rival positions, not successive ages.

## What the texts still cannot say

- **Cameralism and Colbert**: no claims. The German *Polizey* literature is the strongest test of stage 5 as a modern doctrine.
- **The Dutch**: the Republic that was the period's richest market has no voice here (de la Court, Grotius's *Mare liberum*).
- **Bernardino, de Lugo and Lessius**: not held, not held, and 46/806 translated respectively. De Lugo's "just price known only to God" is the strongest stage-3 statement of the market's epistemic edge, and it is unverified.
- **Chinese and Japanese writing after the Han** (Qiu Jun's *Daxue yanyi bu*, Tokugawa merchant ethics) is missing, so the non-European threads stop at 81 BCE and 1377.

title: 2. What this history says to progress studies
md:
**The reader.** The progress-studies field. The field argues over why sustained growth began in north-west Europe around 1750–1850. Four positions are in play, and each makes a claim about *ideas* that primary texts can test:
- **ideas-first**: Mokyr's useful knowledge, Industrial Enlightenment and "culture of growth" ([[1]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-mokyr-2005-baconian-programme) ◐, [[2]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-mokyr-2009-enlightened-economy) ◐), and Jacob's scientific culture ([[3]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-jacob-scientific-culture) ◐);
- **rhetoric-first**: McCloskey's bourgeois dignity ([[4]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-mccloskey-bourgeois-dignity) ◐), with Hirschman's interests taming the passions as its intellectual-history ancestor ([[5]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-hirschman-passions-interests) ◐);
- **institutions-first**: North and Weingast's credible commitment after 1688 ([[6]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-north-weingast-commitment) ◐), against which Clark argues for slow behavioural change ([[7]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-crit-clark-vs-institutions) ◐);
- **prices-first**: Allen's high-wage, cheap-energy economy ([[8]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-allen-high-wage) ◐), contested by Kelly, Mokyr and Ó Gráda on labour quality ([[9]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-kelly-mokyr-ograda-labour-quality) ◐, [[10]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-crit-kelly-vs-allen) ◐).

A fifth, **demand-side**, is de Vries's industrious revolution ([[11]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-devries-industrious-revolution) ◐). The scholarship claims are from abstracts (◐) and say what each author argues, not that it is so.

This page uses only claims in this concept. Every primary-text point is ✓ unless marked.

## 1. "Did the idea come before the change?" splits into two questions with different answers

The question is whether people came to think of the market as a self-ordering, wealth-creating thing before, with or after the economic change. The texts say these are two ideas with two dates.

- **The market as *self-ordering* came before the Industrial Revolution, by about a century in print and four centuries outside Europe.** The English pamphlets of 1690–92 already have a market that corrects itself by exit and by a "natural" rate of interest [[12]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-unprofitable-trade-left-off), [[13]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-locke-natural-interest). Ibn Khaldun had reasoned about tax yields and city prices as an impersonal order around 1377 [[14]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields), [[15]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-city-prices). Smith (1776) illustrates the division of labour with a pin manufactory, not a cotton mill [[16]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-pin-factory); his market sums up a century of argument rather than responding to factories [[17]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-wn-invisible-hand), [[18]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-smith-lj-best-police-natural-course).
- **The market as *open-endedly wealth-creating* came late to political economy, and was not fully accepted there even during the Industrial Revolution.** Smith, Malthus, Ricardo and Mill all keep a *stationary state* (where accumulation stops) as the horizon [[19]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-classical-stationary-horizon), [[20]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-stationary-far-distant), [[21]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-malthus-illimitable-or-oscillation), and Mill (1848) separates growth of wealth, which is bounded, from "human improvement" (the period word, *improvement*: making land, work and knowledge yield more), which is not [[22]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-mill-stationary-state). The open horizon is held instead by the *knowledge* line: Bacon [[23]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-goal-of-sciences), [[24]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-salomons-house), Sprat [[25]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-sprat-saving-hands-riches), the *improvement* writers [[26]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-hartlib-experiment-improvement). A few economic writers outside the Ricardian school also hold it: Barbon [[27]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-national-stock-infinite), Mercier [[28]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/physiocracy#enl-mercier-monde-va-de-lui-meme), Say [[29]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-say-debouches) and List [[30]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-list-industrial-education).

**For the debate:** this supports the ideas-first camp on *where* the growth idea lived (useful knowledge, not price theory), and so fits Mokyr's choice of Bacon as the origin [[1]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-mokyr-2005-baconian-programme) ◐. It cuts against any reading in which *economists'* ideas drove the take-off. The economists theorised a self-ordering market that would come to rest; the people who imagined endless betterment were natural philosophers and projectors. On this evidence, "growth" became thinkable as open-ended in the 1620s–1660s and as an economic expectation only after 1848.

## 2. The re-valuation of trade was long and gradual, not a 17th-century break

McCloskey's thesis needs a change in the *esteem* given to trade and betterment. The texts show esteem moving slowly over two millennia, with the decisive shift as much in the 13th–16th centuries as in the 17th.
- **The objection was narrower than its reputation**, aimed at retail (*kapeleia*, small dealing), *usura* (any gain on a loan) and *chrematistike* (the art of acquisition) without limit, not at exchange [[31]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-arist-pol-shoe-two-uses-exchange-natural), [[32]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/ancient-greek#anc-plato-laws-retail-honourable-if-incorruptible), [[33]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/roman#anc-cicero-off-small-trade-sordid-great-tolerable).
- **Scholastic theology made room for trade** as a "stipend for labour" [[34]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-lucrum-stipend-of-labour), made partnership profit lawful [[35]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-societas-profit-lawful), and let the merchant take "the price he finds" within a just price (*pretium iustum*) set by common estimation [[36]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-seller-price-he-finds).
- **Ibn Khaldun defined commerce without any moral reproach** around 1377 [[37]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-commerce-defined). Poggio's dialogue of 1428 voices the case that cities are "public workshops of avarice", though the dialogue goes on to rebut it [[38]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/merchant-practice#emod-poggio-states-workshops-of-avarice), [[39]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/merchant-practice#emod-poggio-andreas-expel-misers).
- **The old stigma lingered.** In 1640 Saumaise still had to answer "a merchant can never please God" [[40]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-saumaise-negotiator-never-pleases-god).
- **The 1690–1758 change is in *international* esteem**: trade as peace and not as war by other means [[41]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-trade-occasioned-peace), [[42]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-world-one-nation), [[43]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-jealousy-of-trade), and Montesquieu's *doux commerce* (gentle commerce, which softens manners) [[44]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-montesquieu-doux-commerce). It comes with an explicit caveat that commerce unites nations, not persons [[45]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-montesquieu-peace-not-individuals).

**For the debate:** McCloskey is right that the rhetoric changed, but a test that dates the change to 17th-century Holland and England needs to explain why Aquinas, the Salamancans and Ibn Khaldun had already conceded so much. The sharper and more datable shift is from **zero-sum to positive-sum between nations** (1690–1758). Progress-studies writing rarely names that shift, and it is the one a growth culture most obviously needs.

## 3. Institutions: the texts show the problem before they show the solution

North and Weingast make credible commitment after 1688 the key ([[6]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-north-weingast-commitment) ◐). The primary sources are consistent with this in one specific respect: the recurring threat to the market in these texts is the **ruler**, not the merchant.
- Oresme (c. 1355) denies that the prince owns the money and shows coin fleeing debasement [[46]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-money-not-princes), [[47]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-oresme-bullion-flees-debasement).
- Ibn Khaldun (c. 1377) has tax rates destroying the base and a trading ruler crowding out his subjects [[14]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields), [[48]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-ruler-trading-harms).
- Soto condemns royal monopoly privileges [[49]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-soto-monopoly-iniquity); Mariana shows a price ceiling failing [[50]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-mariana-debasement-futile-price-control).
- Locke says the law cannot hold interest below its natural rate [[13]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-locke-natural-interest).
- The Statute of Monopolies of 1624 turns the prince's power to grant privilege into a fourteen-year reward for "the true and first inventor" of new manufactures [[51]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-statute-of-monopolies-new-manufactures): an institutional bridge between the state's market and the improvement line.

**For the debate:** the *diagnosis* that predation by the ruler limits markets is at least four centuries older than 1688 and is not European in origin. What 1688 might add is a remedy, and the primary texts here cannot test that. Fiscal and legal sources would be needed, not treatises.

## 4. Prices-first: the theorists noticed relative prices, but argued about machinery, not wages

Allen's thesis is that dear labour and cheap energy made British invention pay ([[8]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-allen-high-wage) ◐). The contemporary texts do link labour-saving to riches (Sprat 1667 [[25]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-sprat-saving-hands-riches)), and Babbage turns the division of labour into a cost calculation: buy each grade of skill at its own price [[52]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-babbage-principle). But the theorists' live dispute was about **who gains from machinery**: Ricardo's 1821 retraction [[53]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-ricardo-on-machinery), Sismondi's gluts [[54]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-sismondi-engorgement), Ure's factory against "the waywardness of workmen" [[55]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-ure-self-acting-factory), Marx's reply [[56]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-marx-ure-automat-autokrat). **For the debate:** this is evidence of how the change was *experienced* by its theorists. It neither confirms nor refutes Allen's causal story, and should not be quoted as if it did.

## 5. The state's market is the oldest idea here

The *Guanzi*, the Salt and Iron debate and the *Arthashastra* already treat price as a lever of state (*qingzhong*, 'light and heavy'; *pingzhun*, the 'balanced standard') [[57]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-guanzi-qingzhong-no-fixed-number), [[58]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-yantie-comm-pingzhun-buy-cheap-sell-dear), [[59]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/indic#anc-arth-superintendent-commerce-demand-price). The Salt and Iron literati, the opponents of state trading, argued from morals and not from the efficiency of free markets [[60]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#anc-crit-literati-not-laissez-faire) ◐. **For the debate:** "markets versus the state" is not the axis on which growth turned. Han China had sophisticated market policy and a public argument about it, and no sustained growth followed. Whatever was distinctive about Europe c. 1700 was not the discovery that markets respond to prices. That was known in the 4th century BCE.

## 6. Where Polanyi fits

Polanyi argues that the self-regulating market was a 19th-century novelty that had to be imposed (○ [unverified]; unverified, so not used as evidence). The texts here give him the dating of the full doctrine: it is assembled between 1691 and 1776 and is still contested in 1767 [[61]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-steuart-statesman-plan). They also show its pieces much earlier (stage 3 and Ibn Khaldun), which weakens the claim that the idea itself was new.

## The three findings most useful to progress studies

1. **Self-ordering and open-ended growth are separate ideas with separate lineages.** The market was a self-ordering system in print by 1691 and fully by 1776. Open-ended growth lived in the Baconian knowledge line from the 1620s, and classical political economy kept a *stationary state* ceiling until Mill (1848), who then split "wealth" from "improvement". ([[12]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-north-unprofitable-trade-left-off), [[24]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/technology-and-improvement#ind-bacon-salomons-house), [[19]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-classical-stationary-horizon), [[22]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#ind-mill-stationary-state))
2. **The datable change in thinking about trade c. 1690–1760 is from zero-sum to positive-sum between nations**, more than a change in the dignity of the merchant, which had been rising since the 13th century. ([[41]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/political-economy#enl-barbon-trade-occasioned-peace), [[43]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scottish-enlightenment#enl-hume-jealousy-of-trade), [[36]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/scholastic#med-aquinas-seller-price-he-finds), [[37]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-commerce-defined))
3. **Market theory was not the bottleneck.** Price as a lever of state (Guanzi, Han), the tax-yield curve and the crowding-out of subjects by a trading ruler (Ibn Khaldun, c. 1377), and the quantity theory of money (Salamanca, 1550s) were all available long before growth began. ([[57]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/chinese#anc-guanzi-qingzhong-no-fixed-number), [[14]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/islamic#med-ibnkhaldun-tax-rates-yields), [[62]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/salamanca#emod-molina-money-abundance-raises-prices))

## Evidence still missing

- **Dated diffusion.** Who *read* North, Barbon, Cantillon and Hume, and when? Without print runs, editions and citations, "the idea came first" cannot be tested against "the idea was available". This is what Mokyr's "market for ideas" needs (○ [unverified]).
- **Practitioners' expectations.** Engineers', projectors' and investors' writing c. 1750–1830 (Watt, Boulton, Wedgwood, canal and patent literature) would show whether *they*, unlike the economists, expected open-ended growth. Woodcroft's patent index is held.
- **Cameralism, Colbert and the Dutch**: no claims yet. They are the test cases for whether stage 5 was a modern European doctrine or the ancient one restated.
- **The improvement literature in full** (Blith, Arthur Young), and Slack's dating of "improvement" ([[63]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/modern-scholarship#ind-slack-invention-of-improvement) ◐, [[64]](/explore/histories/markets/claims/critique#ind-crit-slack-mokyr-dating-overstated) ◐), checked against the texts rather than the abstract.
- **Non-European writing after 1400.** Ming–Qing political economy and Tokugawa merchant ethics would test whether the "culture of growth" was missing outside Europe or merely untranslated. Nothing here speaks to it yet.
- **Scholarship read in full.** Every modern-scholarship claim here is ◐ from an abstract. Before this page is cited in print, the key passages of Mokyr 2005, McCloskey 2010 and Allen 2009 should be read.
